title.narrative: Thriving communities through women's economic empowerment, improved climate

description.narrative: The ‘Thriving communities through women’s economic empowerment, improved climate resilient livelihoods and the engagement of Civil Society Organisations in Ethiopia’ project aims to empower vulnerable people in two regions within Ethiopia (Oromia and Southern Nations, Nationalities and Peoples) to lift themselves out of poverty through climate adaptive agriculture, business development and establishing civil society organisations. The implementing partners are Wolayita Kale Heywet Church Terepeza Development Association, Meserete Kristos Church Relief and Development Association, and the Consortium of Self Help Group Approach Promoters. The objective is address the economic, social and political dimensions of poverty in order to bring about tangible change for the target beneficiaries, working with households, the community, civil society organisations, and local and regional government. The key activities include localisation and capacity building; building social capital through networks and groups; asset-based Community Development focusing on capacities and capabilities within people and communities; and Church and Community Mobilisation. There is a special emphasis on women, girls and people living with disabilities. In rural areas affected by climate change, the target groups will learn conservation agriculture, sustainable organic agriculture and plant macadamia nuts as an alternative cash crop, which improves climate resilience, livelihoods, food security and nutrition
